title: Drive Plugin Dev/Build Tooling From Cargo.toml Asset/Engine Metadata
description: F5: make dev/build tooling read plugin asset/engine needs from Cargo.toml metadata instead of hardcoding per-app branches. Extend [[package.metadata.semio.playground]] with an `engines` field and add a new [[package.metadata.semio.assets]] table (kinds: tile-proxy, static-dir, mesh-collection). Regenerate framework/plugin/registry/generated/playgrounds.ts with new `engines`/`assets` fields + a PlaygroundAssetSpec TS discriminated union. Update consumers to read this metadata instead of hardcoding: framework/product/os/dev/script.ts (wasm-build loop over engines), framework/product/os/dev/vite.config.ts (optimizeDeps.exclude from registry), ui/styling/vite-elements-assets.ts (collapse bespoke per-app Vite plugins into 3 generic factories + driver), framework/renderer/wgpu/script.ts (generalize GIS-specific tile-proxy bootstrap into generic asset-server bootstrap + rename env var), framework/renderer/wgpu/js/boot.ts (replace hardcoded "-module-procedural" special case with expandPluginRegistry). Add equivalent [[package.metadata.semio.assets]] entries to every existing app plugin Cargo.toml that relied on a hardcoded branch being deleted, preserving identical dev-time behavior.
summary:
Completed the work a prior session left mid-flight (296 tool calls in, stalled on a cargo Monitor wait). Found the core implementation already substantially done via the ticket's `backup/` snapshots; verified every piece against the ticket spec and closed the remaining gap.

Verified already-complete (byte-cross-checked against `backup/*.orig`):
- `framework/plugin/registry/script.ts`: extended with `AssetSpecRow`/`PlaygroundEntry.engines`/`.assets`, TOML block parsing for `[[package.metadata.semio.assets]]`, `PlaygroundAssetSpec` TS union emission.
- `framework/plugin/registry/generated/playgrounds.ts`/`.json`: regenerated (already committed at HEAD) — confirmed byte-identical to what the generator produces from current Cargo.toml metadata via `bun nx run @semio-tech/plugin-registry:check` (passes clean, 32 plugin crates / 34 playgrounds, playground validation clean).
- `framework/product/os/dev/script.ts`: `buildEngineWasm` now resolves engine crates from the playground registry row (`variant.engines`) instead of `if (pluginId === "flow"|"gis2d"|"gis3d"|"raster"|"puzzle2d")` branches.
- `framework/product/os/dev/js/vite.config.ts`: `optimizeDeps.exclude` and dev-time asset plugins now derived from `PLAYGROUND_BUILD_TARGETS` engines/assets instead of hardcoding.
- `ui/styling/vite-elements-assets.ts`: 3 generic Vite plugin factories (`tileProxyVitePlugin`, `staticDirVitePlugin`, `meshCollectionVitePlugin`) + `playgroundAssetVitePlugins` driver replacing the old bespoke per-app plugin functions (cad-fixture, gis tile-proxy, puzzle3d mesh).
- `framework/renderer/wgpu/script.ts`: `ensureGisMapTileProxyServer` → generic `ensureAssetServer` driven by the active variant's `tile-proxy` assets; also fixed a real bug where the old code compared playground *variant* (`"gis2d"`) against *pluginId* (`"gis"`), so it never actually triggered.
- `framework/renderer/wgpu/js/boot.ts`: hardcoded `"${pluginFilter}-module-procedural"` special case replaced by generic `expandPluginRegistry` over `PLUGIN_BUILD_TARGETS` contributes/consumes tags.
- `repo/cli/rs/lib.rs`: Rust mirror of the TS registry generator extended in lockstep (`AssetSpec` struct, `parse_assets_text`, engines field, JSON/TS emission, round-trip parsing, new unit tests) — `rustfmt --check` confirms syntactic validity (only pre-existing wide-line style diffs, present identically in the pre-ticket backup).
- `repo/lib/js/index.ts`: `SEMIO_ASSET_SERVER_PORT`/`SEMIO_ASSET_BASE_URL_ENV` constants, `startAssetServer`.
- Cargo.toml metadata additions matching every removed hardcoded branch: `cad/plugin/rs/Cargo.toml` (static-dir cad-fixture), `gis/plugin/rs/Cargo.toml` (tile-proxy osm/vt/dem scoped per variant), `puzzle/plugin/rs/Cargo.toml` (mesh-collection), `flow/plugin/rs/Cargo.toml` + `raster/plugin/rs/Cargo.toml` (engines rows).
- `framework/renderer/wgpu/rs/Cargo.toml` / `rs/lib.rs`: `SEMIO_GIS_MAP_TILE_BASE_URL` → `SEMIO_ASSET_BASE_URL` env var rename (rest of that file's diff is an unrelated concurrent crate-rename ticket touching the same file — left untouched, out of scope).
- Confirmed no stray references to the removed hardcoded names/branches remain anywhere in the live tree (only doc-comments explaining what was replaced, and a stale `.claude/worktrees/` copy).

Gap found and fixed this session: the new in-source `import.meta.vitest` test coverage added to `ui/styling/vite-elements-assets.ts` (tests for the 3 new generic asset-plugin factories, `resolveGisMapTileServeMode`, etc.) was never wired to any Vitest config — no `vitest.config.ts` existed for `ui/styling` and no `includeSource` anywhere pointed at that file, so all those tests were dead code that had never actually run. Fixed by:
- Adding `ui/styling/vitest.config.ts` (`includeSource`/`include: ["vite-elements-assets.ts"]`, `node` env, aliases `@semio-tech/ui-styling`).
- Registering it in the root `vitest.config.ts` `test.projects` list.
- Adding a `TestScript` (→ `runVitest`) to `ui/styling/script.ts` and a `test` target to `ui/styling/project.json`, following the exact `BundleScript`/`ScriptRouter` pattern used by sibling packages (no `launch.json` change needed — per-project `test` targets are picked up generically by the existing `🧪test🌍workspace` entry, matching convention for every other project's test target).
- Running the now-wired suite surfaced 2 genuine pre-existing failures (dead code, never exercised before): `listMapTilesForBounds` test compared z2 vs z4 tile counts for the Switzerland default bounds, but that bbox still fits in a single OSM tile up to z6 (verified the tile-index math manually) — not an implementation bug, just a bad zoom pair; retargeted the comparison to z2 vs z8. `createWorkspaceViteResolveConfig` test timed out at the 5s default because `findWorkspacePackages` genuinely walks the whole repo tree (~7.5s here) — bumped that one test's timeout to 20s. Neither function is part of this ticket's asset/engine metadata scope; both predate it (present in the pre-ticket `backup/vite-elements-assets.ts.orig`).

Verification performed:
- `bun nx run @semio-tech/plugin-registry:check` — passed clean (registry generator output matches source Cargo.toml metadata exactly).
- `bun nx run @semio-tech/ui-styling-tokens:test` (newly wired) — 38/38 pass after the two fixes above.
- `bun test ui/styling/js/index.test.ts` (separate bun:test suite, unaffected) — 4/4 pass.
- `rustfmt --check` on every touched `.rs` file (`repo/cli/rs/lib.rs`, `framework/core/rs/lib.rs`, `framework/renderer/wgpu/rs/lib.rs`) — all parse as syntactically valid Rust; only cosmetic wide-line diffs pre-existing in this repo's style, confirmed identical in the pre-ticket backup for `repo/cli/rs/lib.rs`.
- `tsc --noEmit` on the full repo (bounded, ran to completion) — 2249 pre-existing errors repo-wide (root `tsconfig.json` lacks `allowImportingTsExtensions`, includes build `dist/` output, lacks Bun globals — none of it specific to this ticket); manually cross-referenced every error in files this ticket touched and confirmed each is either environmental noise (TS5097/`bun:sqlite`/`Bun` global) or on lines untouched by this ticket's diff, pre-dating it.
- Skipped: a full `cargo check --workspace` — deferred to the orchestrator's final gate per instructions (this ticket made no Rust logic changes beyond the Cargo.toml metadata tables and the `repo/cli/rs` mirror, which parses cleanly and is unit-tested).

Not touched (verified out of scope): `framework/core/js/index.ts`'s `expandPluginRegistry`/`PluginRegistryEntry` pre-existed before this ticket (byte-identical to the pre-ticket backup) — some other ticket introduced it; this ticket only consumes it from `boot.ts`. The bulk of `framework/renderer/wgpu/rs/lib.rs`'s diff and the `gis_2d`→`framework/surface/tiled-map` rename in `wgpu/rs/Cargo.toml` belong to a different, concurrent rename ticket touching the same files — left alone.
